chunks: And from him (Al-Husn) from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Hadrami from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon every person who gains or acquires wealth, there is the khums from what they obtain, for Fatimah (peace be upon her) and for the one who manages her affairs after her from her progeny, the proofs upon the people. That is specifically for them; they place it where they wish, because charity (sadaqah) is forbidden for them, so even if a tailor sews a shirt for five dinars, we take one dinar from it, except for whom we permit from our Shias so that lineage becomes pleasing to them through it. Indeed, there is nothing with God on the Day of Resurrection greater than adultery (zina). Indeed, the owner of the khums will stand and say: O Lord, ask these about what was permitted to them.'

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْخُمُسِ: The owner of the khums (one who pays it)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of khums on wealth and who is entitled to receive it according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that khums is a specific right of the Ahl al-Bayt, distinct from general zakat, as they are exempt from receiving ordinary charity but may accept this wealth. The text emphasizes the eschatological weight of khums, noting that the payer will intercede for those who withheld it, while also linking the distribution of khums to facilitating marital ease ('al-wiladah') for the Shia. This underscores the practical and spiritual benefits of khums in sustaining the Imamate and the community.
